diagram_math_checks.check: Using def-brauer-and-partition-diagram-categories: object a has a ordered top inputs and object b has b ordered bottom outputs. I connects one top to one bottom; X pairs top 1 with bottom 2 and top 2 with bottom 1; A pairs its two top inputs and has zero bottom outputs; U pairs its two bottom outputs and has zero top inputs. Thus labels 1→1, 2→2, 2→0, 0→2 agree with the Statement. Intersections have no matching vertices or over/under structure.

U:0→2 followed downward by A:2→0 identifies both U output endpoints with the two A inputs. There is exactly one component with no outer vertices and no boundary matching edges. By the local definition composition removes exactly that component with coefficient δ, giving δ1₀. The single drawn circle and scalar label express exactly this relation, as in Statement and proof step 1.1.

I⊗U maps 1→3; A⊗I maps 3→1. The drawn path runs from the unique top endpoint down its identity segment, along the cap pairing intermediate positions 1 and 2, along the cup pairing positions 2 and 3, then down position 3 to the unique bottom endpoint. It has one outer pair and zero internal closed components, so evaluates to I with coefficient 1. This matches the displayed Statement relation and bending use in step 2.1.

Each composite has type 3→3→1. On the left, the crossing permutes intermediate positions 2 and 3 and the cap consumes positions 1 and 2, joining original top inputs 1 and 3; original top input 2 survives to the bottom. On the right, the crossing swaps positions 1 and 2 and the cap consumes positions 2 and 3, again joining original top inputs 1 and 3 and letting input 2 survive. No closed component occurs in either. The differing horizontal location of the sole bottom endpoint does not change its order. These are exactly the Statement cap-slide relation and the local slide used in proof step 3.1.

The panel illustrates selected stated relations, not an exhaustive graphical replacement for the presentation or cup-train induction. No unpictured braid, reflection or train identity is added as an assumption. The seven original proof steps remain byte-identical and establish the theorem independently of the figure.
